thread:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] cont-batch-worker group 'cb-prod-2' across us-west-2 reporting sudden KV cache growth + request timeouts. p95 token latency > 4s and error rate spiking to 12% :rotating_light:
oncall-tyler: I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking health dashboards.
maria-runtime: hi tyler — paging + KV eviction counters? any correlated evictions?
oncall-tyler: eviction_rate spiked ~x15 starting 3410001100. cont-batch queue depth jumped, worker mem approaching OOM kill thresholds.
ops-bot: Pod restarts detected: rollout/cb-prod-2 replicaset-7f4d -> 5 restarts in last 3m.
jack-eng: any recent config rollouts? maybe batch params or new quantization image?
oncall-tyler: checking deploy history... devdeploy-bot: last configmap apply /namespaces/infra/configmaps/cont-batch-cfg @ 3410000905 by maria-runtime (change: default max_batch_tokens: 1024 -> 65536)
maria-runtime: that change was intended for a dev experiment but should not have hit prod. Investigating how apply reached prod.
oncall-tyler: ok suspected culprit: huge max_batch_tokens increases memory usage + KV cache entries for longer context => eviction/amplification. Need mitigation to restore stability.
oncall-tyler: immediate mitigation option A: roll back configmap to previous values (max_batch_tokens 1024, max_num_seqs 64), option B: temporarily disable continuous batching on cb-prod-2 (toggle to legacy path). Thoughts?
emma-cs: we're seeing customer impact: two enterprise customers reporting increased 5xx and timeouts on embeddings endpoints. ETA for mitigation?
maria-runtime: prefer minimal blast radius — roll back configmap to last known good and reduce max_num_seqs to 32 additionally to avoid batch compaction. Will canary to one AZ first.
oncall-tyler: proceed with rollback canary to us-west-2a, 10% of traffic. I'll patch.

noncall-tyler: ```
kubectl -n infra get configmap cont-batch-cfg -o yaml > /tmp/cont-batch-cfg.pre
kubectl -n infra apply -f /tmp/cont-batch-cfg.rollback.yaml
# rollback file sets: max_batch_tokens: 1024, max_num_seqs: 32, batch_timeout_ms: 50
```

devdeploy-bot: Started rollout of cont-batch-config rollback to cb-prod-2-uswest2a (canary=10%).
incidents-bot: Incident severity -> SEV2. Notifying #incidents and #prod-alerts.
ops-bot: Monitoring evictions, latency, error-rate.

maria-runtime: after rollback canary metrics: p95 latency down from 4.2s -> 0.7s in canary; error-rate back to baseline in that AZ.
oncall-tyler: good. starting staged rollout to remaining AZs.

devdeploy-bot: Rollout to us-west-2b/c completed. New config applied to all replicas.

ops-bot: Pod restarts normalized, eviction_rate trending to baseline, cont-batch queue draining.

emma-cs: messaging plan: sending a brief note to affected customers: "We've identified a config change causing KV cache amplification; mitigated and rolled back; working on RCA; contact support for details." Want to include timeline and ETA for RCA.
jack-eng: need a post-incident hotfix to prevent this class of mistake: add automated gating that prevents experimental configmap keys from being promoted to prod without a 'promote=true' label and add a validation check in CI for max_batch_tokens > 8192.
maria-runtime: agreed. Also will add a runtime guard to reject config changes where max_batch_tokens > 8192 unless override token provided.
oncall-tyler: I'm adding short-term circuit: if eviction_rate > 5x baseline, autoset max_batch_tokens=1024 automatically.

sri-oncall: taking handoff in 30m — summary pls?
oncall-tyler: summary: root cause suspected mis-applied config change increased max_batch_tokens 1024->65536. This caused KV cache to retain much larger batches, memory pressure, evictions, and continuous-batch queue growth -> higher latencies and 5xx for some customers. Mitigation: rolled back configmap to conservative values (max_batch_tokens=1024, max_num_seqs=32, batch_timeout_ms=50) via canary then full rollout. Metrics returned to baseline.
emma-cs: impacted customers notified. No escalations to legal required at this time.

incidents-bot: Assigning follow-up ticket: INC-341000-ctb-config-rollback for RCA and action items. Assignee: maria-runtime.
maria-runtime: I'll own RCA and follow-ups. Immediate action items: 1) CI validation for config thresholds, 2) runtime guard to auto-limit batch params on eviction spikes, 3) audit deploy pipeline to understand how experimental change reached prod, 4) update runbook.

jack-eng: quick note: we also observed a pathological case where large max_batch_tokens increased per-batch KV writes which caused KVS compaction thrash. I'll put a perf test to simulate large batch_token values.

sri-oncall: taking over. If any regression or customer reports come in ping me directly. I'll coordinate postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 PT.
emma-cs: I'll prep customer communication and leave a follow-up thread in #customer-success with affected org list.

noncall-tyler: leaving on-call now — monitoring alerts cleared. Handing to sri-oncall. :white_check_mark:
maria-runtime: pushing initial RCA draft to the incident ticket.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated. Postmortem required (P2 -> documentation + prevent recurrence).

sri-oncall: adding this to tomorrow's oncall rota review. Thanks team. :coffee:
